_doc: Adapter-specific overlay on Next.js's own test/deploy-tests-manifest.json, merged by
Version-2 semantics: `suites.<file>.failed[]` holds FULL test names, which the runner turns
into a negated --testNamePattern; `rules.exclude[]` drops whole files before they are built.
Both merge additively with upstream's entries, and an exact-filename exclude wins over an
inclusion. Unknown keys (like this one) are ignored by the parser.
ONLY record a failure here once its cause is understood and is NOT an adapter correctness
bug. Anything listed stops being visible, so every entry needs a narrow, durable reason.

_reason: The adapter is MORE correct than the deploy target this expectation was written for.
Upstream's own comment marks the Vercel behaviour as the deviation, and the test asserts
it. The adapter does a blocking revalidation when the entry has expired, which is what
`expire` means; asserting otherwise would mean regressing to match a known-wrong target.
Deploy and build both succeed here — only the assertion diverges — so this is a
case-level exclusion rather than a file exclusion.
failed: expire-time should do a blocking revalidation when the cache entry has expired

_reason: These two fixtures store counters in mutable module globals and require separate HTTP
requests to reuse one process. The deployed adapter deliberately runs two replicas; pod
logs prove the requests can reach different replicas, each correctly returning its own
first increment. Next's action-worker forwarding does not provide replica affinity.
Single-process conformance still runs both cases.

_reason: This isNextDeploy-only assertion requires durable materialization of a shell-less
fallback:null PPR entry. The adapter's Option-D path resumes it correctly, but currently
retains only the callback's postponed state; it does not validate and atomically persist
the complete APP_PAGE entry in Valkey for another replica. Adding raw response replay
would be unsafe because its key omits cookies, authorization, and personalization inputs.
The other three OTel/cache lifecycle assertions remain enabled.

test/e2e/app-dir/next-dist-client-esm-im: Upstream Turbopack panic, not an adapter failure: the BUILD aborts with
`FATAL: An unexpected Turbopack error occurred` and writes a Rust panic log, failing to

parse ordinary JSX (`return

hello world

;`) in the fixture. Excluded at FILE level
rather than case level because the deploy never completes — a case exclusion would still
pay for the build and still emit a panic log every run.
